forecaster_note: Winds go offshore and S and NE swell mix cleans up. Head to overhead. Head to OH sets at the south magnets. Powerful, but with waits between the sets. A notch smaller elsewhere. Clean this morning with light variable to offshore winds but still some wobble and jumble to it as NE wind wave gets in. NE winds expected to pick up mid-morning and most spots trend junky. Sheltered northern corners stay cleanest. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: WNW offshore 4kph at dawn — clean start. Swings NE onshore by mid-morning (16–20kph) and builds to 20–30kph gusting through the afternoon.

shark.summary: No shark detections anywhere between Palm Beach and Manly in the past 24h — Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl and Manly all clear. Nearest recent: an SLS drone sighting at Freshwater Beach at 7:22am Sun 20 Sep, about 73h ago. Feed confirmed live — newest statewide detection 24 minutes ago, 65 real detections statewide in the last 24h.

days.label: Today
days.note: Genuine mixed swell for once — a 71° ENE windswell (5.6ft @ 6s) squares up nicely on the NE beaches while a long-period S groundswell (17s @ 181°) still feeds the reef at Long Reef. WNW offshore at dawn swings NE onshore by mid-morning, so 6–9am is the window. Long Reef's the standout at 3–6ft Fair-Good; the rest sit around Fair.

dee-why.window: 6–9am — WNW offshore and the ENE component lines up nicely at the Point before the NE sea breeze fills in and swings it onshore around 10am.
alerts: NE onshore builds through the morning — 16kph by 9am, 20–30kph gusting by early afternoon

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 71° puts real E in this swell — a big step up from the dead-S wrap you've been getting. The Point should line up properly again; take the rights frontside and expect a bit of extra push on sets from the long-period S groundswell still running underneath.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 9am — light offshore, and the point's getting both the fresher NE windswell and a lingering long-period S groundswell. Best all-round spot today.
alerts: Best-rated spot on the coast today (Fair–Good) — the south-facing reef is picking up both swell trains

tip.label: Frontside off the point
tip.text: South-facing, so it's still hoovering up the long-period S groundswell (17s @ 181°) for the point surf — but today it's also wrapping in the fresher ENE windswell. That combination is why this is rating above Dee Why and Curl Curl. Frontside rights, expect some size on the bigger sets.

curl-curl.window: 6–9am for the cleanest of it — south corner still the pick as the NE swell fills in.
alerts: Wind swings onshore/cross-shore by mid-morning — go early

tip.label: Both ways off the banks
tip.text: Picking up the same mixed swell as the other spots — the ENE component squares up better on the banks than a pure S day would, so expect more rideable peaks than usual. Lefts backside off the south corner; shorter board to stay reactive.

manly.window: 9am–12pm, smallest and most sheltered — the fallback if the other three get too onshore.
alerts: Sheltered from the bulk of the swell — only 2–4ft while Long Reef runs 3–6ft

tip.label: North Steyne banks
tip.text: E-facing corner takes a bit of the ENE component square-on today, so it should be a touch livelier than a straight S day. Grovel volume, take what the banks give you.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: NE swell holds respectable size (2–5ft) but the wind's the problem — light and cross-shore at dawn, then a 24–26kph NE sea breeze takes over by mid-morning and flattens the session. Long Reef's the only spot rating Fair; get in early or wait for the weekend.

dee-why.window: Dawn to 8am before the NE breeze fills in hard — after that it's a write-off.

long-reef.window: Dawn to 9am, the pick of the day at 3–5ft — still holding some shape before the sea breeze wrecks it.

curl-curl.window: Dawn only, 6–8am — onshore chop takes over fast.

manly.window: Dawn to 9am if you want small and sheltered from the worst of the breeze.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday's the pick — clean NE swell, light offshore morning, Fair across the board at 2–4ft. A bigger S swell (4–8ft) fills in for Sunday but the wind goes hard onshore S/SSE all day (20–25kph) — skip it unless you just want a paddle.

dee-why.window: Saturday 7–10am — NW offshore easing to light onshore by midday, cleanest window of the weekend.

long-reef.window: Saturday dawn–10am. NE swell wraps in nicely — best size-to-quality trade of the weekend.

curl-curl.window: Saturday 7–10am, peaky NE swell on the beachies with a light offshore start.

manly.window: Saturday mid-morning — small, clean, and the most protected from Sunday's mess.
